units.literal: Yet your servant's grandfather, at the end of Tianbao, having no other path to office, reluctantly followed the examination route and passed in a single attempt.

units.zh: 自後家不置《文選》，蓋惡其不根藝實。
units.en: Afterward our family kept no copy of the Wenxuan, for we despised its lack of grounding in genuine learning.
units.literal: Afterward the family kept no copy of the Wenxuan, for they detested its lack of grounding in real learning.

units.zh: 然朝廷顯官，須公卿子弟為之。
units.en: Yet prominent offices at court ought to be filled by sons of high ministers.
units.literal: Yet prominent offices at court ought to be filled by sons of high ministers.

units.zh: 何者？
units.en: Why?
units.literal: Why?

units.zh: 少習其業，目熟朝廷事，台閣之儀，不教而自成。
units.en: From youth they practice statecraft, grow familiar with court affairs, and learn the etiquette of the secretariat and chancellery without formal instruction.
units.literal: From youth they practice that profession, their eyes familiar with court affairs and the etiquette of the secretariat and chancellery—they master it without being taught.

units.zh: 寒士縱有出人之才，固不能閑習也。
units.en: Poor scholars, however gifted, cannot acquire such familiarity in their spare time.
units.literal: Poor scholars, even with outstanding talent, certainly cannot acquire such familiarity in leisure.

units.zh: 則子弟未易可輕。」
units.en: Thus the sons of officials are not to be lightly dismissed."
units.literal: Thus sons of officials are not easily to be slighted."

units.zh: 德裕之論，偏異蓋如此。
units.en: Li Deyu's argument was partial and eccentric in roughly this fashion.
units.literal: Li Deyu's argument was partial and eccentric in roughly this fashion.

units.zh: 然進士科當唐之晚節，尤為浮薄，世所共患也。
units.en: Yet in the late Tang the Jinshi examination had grown especially frivolous and shallow—a malady universally lamented.
units.literal: Yet the Jinshi examination in the late phase of Tang was especially frivolous and shallow—a common affliction of the age.

units.zh: 所謂制舉者，其來遠矣。
units.en: The decree examination, as it was called, had ancient roots.
units.literal: What is called the decree examination has a distant origin.

units.zh: 自漢以來，天子常稱制詔道其所欲問而親策之。
units.en: Since Han times, emperors often issued edicts in their own name stating the topics they wished to examine and personally tested candidates on them.
units.literal: From Han onward, the Son of Heaven often issued edicts in his own name stating what he wished to ask and personally examined candidates on it.

units.zh: 唐興，世崇儒學，雖其時君賢愚好惡不同，而樂善求賢之意未始少怠，故自京師外至州縣，有司常選之士，以時而舉。
units.en: When the Tang arose, the empire honored Confucian learning. Although individual rulers differed in wisdom and taste, the desire to seek worthy men never slackened. From the capital to prefectures and counties, officials regularly selected scholars and presented them at the proper seasons.
units.literal: When Tang arose, the age honored Confucian learning; although rulers differed in wisdom and folly and in likes and dislikes, the intent to delight in goodness and seek the worthy never slackened, and so from the capital outward to prefectures and counties, the offices regularly selected scholars and presented them at the proper seasons.

units.zh: 而天子又自詔四方德行、才能、文學之士，或高蹈幽隱與其不能自達者，下至軍謀將略、翹關拔山、絕藝奇伎莫不兼取。
units.en: The emperor also personally summoned from all directions men of virtue, talent, and literary accomplishment—including recluses who could not advance on their own—and extended his search to military strategists, strongmen, and masters of exceptional skills: none were excluded.
units.literal: The Son of Heaven also personally summoned from the four directions men of virtue, talent, and literary accomplishment—or those who lived in lofty seclusion and could not advance on their own—down to military stratagem and generalship, gate-lifting and mountain-pulling, and supreme skills and strange arts: none were excluded.

units.zh: 其為名目，隨其人主臨時所欲，而列為定科者，如賢良方正、直言極諫、博通墳典達於教化、軍謀宏遠堪任將率、詳明政術可以理人之類，其名最著。
units.en: Designations varied with each ruler's wishes. Those established as regular categories included Worthy and Good and Upright, Straightforward and Extreme Remonstrance, Broad Mastery of the Classics and Attainment in Civilizing Instruction, Grand and Far-Reaching Military Strategy Fit to Command Armies, and Detailed Understanding of Government Techniques Able to Order the People—these were the most prominent names.
units.literal: The designations varied with what the ruler at the time desired; those fixed as regular categories included Worthy and Good, Straightforward and Outspoken Remonstrance, Broad Mastery of the Classics and Attainment in Civilizing Instruction, Grand Military Strategy Fit to Command Armies, and Clear Mastery of Government Able to Order the People—these names were most prominent.

units.zh: 而天子巡狩、行幸、封禪太山梁父，往往會見行在，其所以待之之禮甚優，而宏材偉論非常之人亦時出於其間，不為無得也。
units.en: When the emperor toured the realm, traveled, or performed the feng and shan sacrifices on Mount Tai and Liangfu, candidates often met him at his traveling court and were treated with exceptional courtesy. Great talents and extraordinary men sometimes emerged from these occasions, and the system was not without benefit.
units.literal: When the Son of Heaven made inspection tours, traveled, or performed the feng and shan sacrifices on Mount Tai and Liangfu, candidates often met him at his traveling court; the courtesy shown them was very generous, and great talents with weighty discourse and extraordinary men sometimes emerged among them—it was not without gain.

units.zh: 其外，又有武舉，蓋其起于武后之時。
units.en: Beyond these, there was also the military examination, which originated in the time of Empress Wu.
units.literal: Beyond these, there was also the military examination, which originated roughly in the time of Empress Wu.

units.zh: 長安二年，始置武舉。
units.en: In 702, the military examination was first established.
units.literal: In the second year of Chang'an, the military examination was first established.

units.zh: 其制，有長垛、馬射、步射、平射、筒射，又有馬槍、翹關、負重、身材之選。
units.en: The regulations included long-range target shooting, mounted archery, foot archery, level shooting, and tube shooting, as well as lance work from horseback, gate-lifting, weight-bearing, and physique assessment.
units.literal: Its regulations included long-range target shooting, mounted archery, foot archery, level shooting, and tube shooting; also lance from horseback, gate-lifting, weight-bearing, and physique selection.

units.zh: 翹關，長丈七尺，徑三寸半，凡十舉後，手持關距，出處無過一尺；
units.en: For gate-lifting, the bar was one zhang seven chi long and three and a half cun in diameter. After ten lifts, the bar's rise and fall at the grip could not exceed one chi;
units.literal: For gate-lifting, the bar was one zhang seven chi long and three and a half cun in diameter; after ten lifts in all, holding the bar at the grip, the rise and fall might not exceed one chi;

units.zh: 負重者，負米五斛，行二十步：皆為中第，亦以鄉飲酒禮送兵部。
units.en: for weight-bearing, carrying five hu of rice for twenty paces. All counted as a passing grade and were forwarded to the Ministry of War with the district drinking ceremony.
units.literal: for weight-bearing, carrying five hu of rice and walking twenty paces: all counted as middle grade, and they were also sent to the Ministry of War with the district drinking ceremony.

units.zh: 其選用之法不足道，故不復書。
units.en: The methods of selection and appointment are not worth recounting here, and so they are not recorded further.
units.literal: The methods of selection and appointment were not worth recounting, and so they are not recorded further.

units.zh: 尚書敬顯儁曰：「孔子云：『微管仲，吾其被發左衽矣』以此言之，右衽為是。」
units.en: Minister Jing Xianjun said, "Confucius said, 'Were it not for Guan Zhong, we would wear our hair loose and our lapel to the left.' By this reasoning the right lapel is correct."
units.literal: Minister Jing Xianjun said, "Confucius said, 'Were it not for Guan Zhong, we would wear our hair loose and our lapel to the left.' By this reasoning the right lapel is correct."

units.zh: 伏願陛下哀忠念舊，愛孤恤寡，矜愚嘉善，舍過記功，敦骨肉之情，廣寬仁之路，思堯、舜之風，慕禹、湯之德，克己復禮，以成美化，天下幸甚。」
units.en: I venture to hope Your Majesty will pity the loyal and remember the old, cherish the orphaned and comfort the widowed, pity the foolish and praise the good, pardon faults and record merit, thicken kinship among flesh and bone, broaden the path of generous forbearance, think of the manner of Yao and Shun, admire the virtue of Yu and Tang, restrain yourself and return to ritual to complete a transformation of culture — all under Heaven would be greatly blessed."
units.literal: I venture to hope Your Majesty will pity the loyal and remember the old, cherish the orphaned and comfort the widowed, pity the foolish and praise the good, pardon faults and record merit, thicken kinship among flesh and bone, broaden the path of generous forbearance, think of the manner of Yao and Shun, admire the virtue of Yu and Tang, restrain yourself and return to ritual, to complete a transformation of culture — all under Heaven would be greatly blessed."

units.zh: 履冰又上奏曰：臣聞夫婦之道，人倫之始。尊卑法於天地，動靜合於陰陽，陰陽和而天地生成，夫婦正而人倫式序。自家刑國，牝雞無晨，四德之禮不愆，三從之義斯在。即《喪服四制》云：「天無二日，土無二王，國無二君，家無二尊，以一理之也。故父在為母服周者，見無二尊也。」准舊儀，父在為母一週除靈，再周心喪。父必三年而後娶者，達子之志焉。豈先聖無情於所生，固有意於家國者矣。原夫上元肇年，則天已潛秉政，將圖僭篡，預自崇先。請升慈愛之喪，以抗尊嚴之禮，雖齊斬之儀不改，而几筵之制遂同。數年之間，尚未通用。天皇晏駕，中宗蒙塵。垂拱之末，果行聖母之偽符；載初之元，遂啟易代之深釁。孝和雖名反正，韋氏復效晨鳴。孝和非意暴崩，韋氏旋即稱制。不蒙陛下英算，宗廟何由克復？《易》云：「臣弒其君，子弒其父，非一朝一夕之故。」其斯之謂矣。臣謹尋禮意，防杜實深，若不早圖刊正，何以垂戒於後？所以薄言禮教，請依舊章，恩敕通明，蒙付所司詳議。且臣所獻者，蓋請正夫婦之綱，豈忘母子之道。諸議多不討其本源，所非議者，大凡只論罔極之恩；喪也寧戚；禽獸識母而不識父；秦燔書後禮經殘缺，後儒纘集，不足可憑；豈得與伯叔母服同，豈得與姑姊妹制等；三王不相襲禮，五帝不相沿樂；齊斬足為升降，歲年何忍不同：此並道聽途說之言，未習先王之旨，又安足以議經邦理俗之禮乎？臣請據經義以明之。所云「罔極之恩」者，春秋祭祀，以時思之。君子有終身之憂，霜露之感，豈止一二周之服哉！故聖人恐有朝死而夕忘，曾鳥獸之不若，為立中制，使賢不肖共成文理而已。所云「喪也寧戚」者，孔子答林放之問。至如太奢太儉，太易太戚，皆非禮中。苟不得中，名為俱失，不如太儉太戚焉。毀而滅性，猶愈於朝死夕忘焉。此論臨喪哀毀之容，豈比於同宗異姓之服？所云「禽獸識母而不識父」者，禽獸群居而聚筜，而無家國之禮，少雖知親愛其母，長不解尊嚴其父。引此為諭則亦禽獸之不若乎！所云「秦燔書後禮經殘缺，後儒纘集，不足可憑」者，人間或有遺逸，豈亦家戶到而燔之？假若盡燔，苟不可信，則墳黃都謬，庠序徒立，非聖之談，復云安屬？所云「與伯叔姑姊服同」者，伯叔姑姊有筵杖之制、三年心喪乎？所云「五帝不相沿樂，不相襲禮」，誠哉是言！此是則天懷私苞禍之情，豈可復相沿樂襲禮乎？所云「齊斬足為升降」者，母齊父斬，不易之禮。按《三年問》云：「將由修飾之君子與，三年之喪，若駟之過隙，遂之，則是無窮也。然則何以周也？曰：至親以周斷。是何也？曰：天地則已易矣，四時則已變矣，其在天地之者，莫不更始焉，以是象之也。然則何以三年？曰：加重焉耳。」故父加至再周，父在為母加三年心喪。今者還同父沒之制，則尊厭之律安施？《喪服四制》又曰：「凡禮之大體，體天地，法四時，則陰陽，順人情，故謂之禮。」訾之者是不知禮之所由生。非徒不識禮之所由制，亦恐未達孝子之通義。臣謹按《孝經》，以明陛下孝治之合至德要道，請論世欲訾禮之徒。夫至德謂孝悌，要道謂禮樂。「移風易俗，莫善於樂，安上治民，莫善於禮。」又《禮》有「無體之禮，無聲之樂。」按《孝經援神契》云：「天子孝曰就，就之為言成也。天子德被天下，澤及萬物，始終成就，則其親獲安，故曰就也。諸侯孝曰度，度者法也。諸侯居國，能奉天子法度，得不危溢，則其親獲安，故曰度也。卿大夫孝曰譽，譽之為言名也。卿大夫言行佈滿，能無惡稱，譽達遐邇，則其親獲安，故曰譽也。士孝曰究，究者以明審為義。士始升朝，辭親入仕，能審資父事君之禮，則其親獲安，故曰究也。庶人孝曰畜，畜者含畜為義。庶人含情受朴，躬耕力作，以畜其德，則其親獲安，故曰畜也。」陛下以韋氏構逆，中宗降禍，宸衷哀憤，睿情卓烈。初無一旅之眾，遂殄九重之妖，定社稷於阽危，拯宗枝於塗炭。此陛下孝悌之至，通於神明，光於四海，無所不通。使諸侯得守其法度，卿大夫得盡其言行，士得資親以事君，庶人得用天而分地。此陛下無體之禮，以安上理人也。上元以來，政由武氏，文明之後，法在凶人。賊害宗親，誅滅良善，勳階歲累，酺赦年頻。佞之則榮華，正之則遷謫。神龍、景雲之際，其事尤繁；先天、開元之間，斯弊都革。此陛下之無聲之樂，以移風易俗也。臣前狀單略，議者未識臣之懇誠。謹具狀重進，請付中書門下商量處分。臣言若讜，然敢側足於軒墀；臣言不忠，伏請竄跡於荒裔。
units.en: Lu Lubing again submitted a memorial: Your servant has heard that the way of husband and wife is the beginning of human relations. Honored and lowly take law from Heaven and earth; movement and stillness accord with yin and yang. When yin and yang are harmonious, Heaven and earth generate and complete; when husband and wife are correct, human relations are thereby ordered. From regulating the family to governing the state, the hen has no morning cry; the rites of the four virtues do not fail, and the obligation of the three followings is here. The Four Mourning Systems says: "Heaven has no two suns, earth has no two kings, the state has no two rulers, and the household has no two honored ones; these are ordered by one principle. Therefore when the father is alive, one wears one-year mourning for the mother, showing that there are not two honored ones." According to the old ritual, when the father was alive, for the mother one removed the spirit seat after one cycle and observed inner mourning for two cycles. That the father must wait three years before marrying again expresses the son's intent. How could the former sages have had no feeling for the one who gave birth, when they were certainly intent on household and state? Looking back, in the first year of Shangyuan, Zetian had already secretly taken hold of government. Planning usurpation, she first honored her ancestors. She requested raising compassionate mourning to oppose the rites of reverence; although the forms of trimmed and unhemmed mourning were not changed, the system of mats and seats became the same. For several years it still was not generally used. The Heavenly Emperor died, and Zhongzong suffered dust and exile. At the end of Chuigong, the false tally of the Sage Mother was indeed carried out; in the first year of Zaichu, the deep provocation for changing dynasties was opened. Although Xiaohe was called a return to correctness, the Wei clan again imitated the morning cry. Xiaohe suddenly died contrary to expectation, and the Wei clan immediately took charge. Had it not been for Your Majesty's heroic planning, how could the ancestral temples have been restored? The Changes says: "When a minister murders his ruler or a son murders his father, it is not the cause of one morning or one evening." This is what it means. Your servant has carefully sought the meaning of ritual, and its guard and prevention are truly deep. If we do not early plan to cut and correct this, how can we transmit warning to later times? Therefore I briefly spoke of ritual teaching and requested following the old statutes. The gracious edict was penetrating and clear, and I received referral to the responsible offices for detailed deliberation. What your servant submitted was a request to correct the bond of husband and wife; how could it forget the way of mother and son? Most deliberations do not examine the root and source. What they criticize generally only discusses boundless grace, that in mourning one should prefer grief, that birds and beasts know their mothers but not their fathers, that after Qin burned the books the ritual classics were damaged and later Confucians compiled them and are not reliable, that how could it be the same mourning as for paternal uncles' wives, how could it equal the rules for paternal aunts and sisters, that the Three Kings did not inherit one another's rites and the Five Emperors did not follow one another in music, and that trimmed and unhemmed garments are enough for increase and reduction while one cannot bear for the years to differ. These are all words heard on the road, not practiced in the former kings' intent. How are they enough to discuss the rites that order the state and regulate custom? Your servant requests to rely on classic meaning to clarify it. As for what is called "boundless grace," spring and autumn sacrifices remember it by season. A gentleman has lifelong grief and the feeling of frost and dew; how could it stop with one or two cycles of mourning dress? Therefore sages feared that some would have a morning death and evening forgetfulness, worse than birds and beasts, and established a middle regulation, so that worthy and unworthy together completed pattern and principle. As for what is called "in mourning, prefer grief," this is Confucius answering Lin Fang's question. As for too extravagant and too frugal, too easy and too grief-stricken, all are not within the ritual mean. If one cannot attain the mean, both are called losses, though too frugal and too grief-stricken are better. Destroying oneself and extinguishing one's nature is still better than morning death and evening forgetfulness. This discusses the appearance of grief and self-damage when facing mourning; how can it be compared to mourning dress for the same lineage and different surnames? As for "birds and beasts know the mother but not the father," birds and beasts live in flocks and gather without the rites of household and state. When young, they may know to love their mothers, but when grown they do not understand honoring their fathers. If this is cited as an analogy, are we not worse than birds and beasts? As for "after Qin burned the books, the ritual classics were damaged, and later Confucians compiled them, so they cannot be relied upon," among people there may have been texts left or lost; did Qin burn them from house to house? Suppose they were all burned. If they cannot be trusted, then the ancient classics are all mistaken, schools stand in vain, and to what does talk that rejects the sages belong? As for "the same mourning as paternal uncles' wives and paternal aunts and sisters," do paternal uncles' wives, paternal aunts, and sisters have a system of mats and staffs or three years of inner mourning? As for "the Five Emperors did not follow one another in music and did not inherit one another's rites," true indeed are these words! This was Zetian's feeling of harboring selfishness and wrapping disaster; how could one again follow her music and inherit her rite? As for "trimmed and unhemmed are enough for increase and reduction," trimmed for mother and unhemmed for father is unchanging ritual. According to Questions on Three Years: "Is it because of cultivated gentlemen? Three years of mourning is like a team of four horses passing a crack; if one extended it, it would be endless. Then why stop with one year? It says: the closest kin are cut off by a year. Why is this? It says: Heaven and earth have already changed; the four seasons have already changed; among what is within Heaven and earth, nothing has not begun anew, and this is used to model it. Then why three years? It says: weight is added." Therefore for the father it is increased to two full cycles, and while the father is alive, for the mother it is increased by three years of inner mourning. If now it is returned to the rule for when the father has died, where will the law of honored suppression be applied? The Four Mourning Systems also says: "In general, the great body of ritual embodies Heaven and earth, takes law from the four seasons, follows yin and yang, and accords with human feeling; therefore it is called ritual." Those who criticize this do not know from what ritual is born. Not only do they not understand from what ritual is made; I also fear they have not grasped the general obligation of a filial son. Your servant has carefully examined the Classic of Filial Piety to make clear that Your Majesty's filial governance accords with utmost virtue and the essential way, and I request to discuss those in the age who wish to criticize ritual. Utmost virtue means filial piety and fraternal respect; the essential way means rites and music. "For changing customs, nothing is better than music; for securing superiors and governing the people, nothing is better than ritual." Also, the Ritual has "formless ritual and soundless music." According to the Filial Piety apocryphon Yuan Shen Qi: "The Son of Heaven's filial piety is called completion; completion means accomplishing. When the Son of Heaven's virtue covers All Under Heaven and his grace reaches the myriad things, beginning and end are accomplished, and then his parents obtain peace; therefore it is called completion. A feudal lord's filial piety is called measure; measure means law. When a feudal lord resides in his state and can uphold the Son of Heaven's laws and measures, not becoming endangered or overflowing, then his parents obtain peace; therefore it is called measure. A minister or great officer's filial piety is called reputation; reputation means name. When a minister or great officer's words and conduct spread fully and can have no evil name, and his reputation reaches far and near, then his parents obtain peace; therefore it is called reputation. A shi's filial piety is called investigation; investigation takes clarity and examination as its meaning. When a shi first enters court, leaves his parents and enters service, and can examine the rite of using the father as resource to serve the ruler, then his parents obtain peace; therefore it is called investigation. A commoner's filial piety is called storing up; storing up takes containing and preserving as its meaning. When a commoner contains feeling and receives simplicity, personally plowing and laboring in order to store up his virtue, then his parents obtain peace; therefore it is called storing up." Because the Wei clan plotted rebellion and Zhongzong suffered disaster, Your Majesty's imperial heart was grieved and angered, and your sagely feeling was outstanding and fierce. At first you had not even one brigade of troops, yet you destroyed the monster in the ninefold palace, fixed the altars of soil and grain in danger, and rescued the imperial branches from mire and ashes. This is the utmost of Your Majesty's filial piety and fraternal respect, penetrating to spirits and brightness, shining over the four seas, with nothing it does not reach. It lets feudal lords keep their laws and measures, ministers and great officers exhaust their words and conduct, shi use kinship to serve the ruler, and commoners use Heaven and divide earth. This is Your Majesty's formless ritual, by which you secure superiors and order the people. Since Shangyuan, government came from the Wu clan; after Wenming, law lay with cruel people. They harmed imperial kin, killed the good, accumulated merit ranks every year, and frequently held feasts and amnesties. To flatter them brought glory; to correct them brought demotion and exile. During Shenlong and Jingyun, these affairs were especially numerous; between Xiantian and Kaiyuan, these abuses were all reformed. This is Your Majesty's soundless music, by which you changed customs. Your servant's previous statement was brief, and the debaters did not understand my earnest sincerity. I have carefully prepared this statement and present it again, requesting that it be sent to the Secretariat-Chancellery for deliberation and disposition. If your servant's words are honest, then I dare stand beside the palace steps. If your servant's words are not loyal, I humbly request exile to the distant borders.

units.en: Li Deyu then memorialized, "Both Chen Xingtai and Zhang Jiang had their generals petition the throne demanding commissions — for that reason they must on no account be granted.
units.literal: Li Deyu thereupon memorialized: "Chen Xingtai and Zhang Jiang both had great generals submit memorials to demand seals and credentials — therefore they must on no account be granted.

units.zh: 仲武由是威加北狄，表請於薊北立《紀聖功銘》，敕李德裕為之文，其銘曰：太和之初，赤氣宵興；
units.en: Zhongwu's prestige over the northern peoples was now supreme. He memorialized asking that a Record of Sacred Merit stele be erected north of Ji, and the court ordered Li Deyu to compose the inscription, which reads: In early Taihe crimson vapors rose at night;
units.literal: Zhongwu thereby gained authority over the northern barbarians; he memorialized requesting that a "Record of Sacred Merit" stele be erected north of Ji, and an edict ordered Li Deyu to compose the text. The inscription reads: At the beginning of Taihe, crimson vapors rose through the night;

units.zh: 今仲武上表布誠，先陳密款，因而拔用，即似有名。」
units.en: Zhongwu has now memorialized the throne with a pledge of loyalty, offering his allegiance in advance. To appoint him on that basis would seem legitimate."
units.literal: Now Zhongwu has submitted a memorial declaring his loyalty, first setting forth a secret pledge of allegiance; to promote him on that basis would seem justified."

units.zh: 開成之末，彤雲暮凝。
units.en: By the close of Kaicheng rosy clouds hung thick at dusk.
units.literal: At the end of Kaicheng, rosy clouds congealed at dusk.

units.zh: 異鳥南來，胡滅之征。
units.en: Strange birds flew from the south, portending the barbarians' destruction.
units.literal: Strange birds came from the south — a sign that the barbarians would be destroyed.

units.zh: 北夷飈掃，厥國土崩。
units.en: Northern tribes were swept away in a whirlwind, and their realm collapsed.
units.literal: Northern tribes were swept away like a storm; their state collapsed.

units.zh: 逼迫遷徙，震我邊鄙；
units.en: Driven into migration, they shook our frontier lands;
units.literal: Driven and forced to migrate, they shook our frontier districts;

units.zh: 會昌初，陳行泰殺節度使史元忠，權主留後。
units.en: Early in the Huichang era Chen Xingtai killed the military governor Shi Yuanzhong and seized control as acting administrator.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Huichang reign, Chen Xingtai killed the military governor Shi Yuanzhong and held the acting administrator's post on his own authority.

units.zh: 按唐開元中，玄宗詔曰：「祀神以玉，取其精潔，比來用瑉，不可行也。
units.en: In Kaiyuan of Tang, Emperor Xuanzong decreed: "Spirits are worshipped with jade for its purity and refinement; the recent use of min stone cannot be permitted.
units.literal: According to Kaiyuan of Tang, Emperor Xuanzong decreed: "To sacrifice to the spirits with jade is to take its purity and refinement; recently min stone has been used—this cannot be permitted.

units.zh: 兼冊文內有『基』字，是玄宗廟諱，雖尋常詔敕皆不回避，少帝是繼世之孫，不欲斥列聖之諱，今改『基』為『宗』字。」
units.en: Moreover, the writ contains the character 'ji,' the temple taboo of Emperor Xuanzong; although ordinary edicts do not avoid it, the Lesser Emperor is a descendant in succession and we do not wish to pronounce the taboos of successive sages—'ji' is now changed to 'zong.'"
units.literal: Moreover, within the writ text is the character 'ji,' which is the temple taboo of Emperor Xuanzong; although ordinary edicts do not avoid it, the Lesser Emperor is a descendant in succession and we do not wish to pronounce the taboos of successive sages—now 'ji' is changed to the character 'zong."

units.zh: 今昭宣上去玄宗十四世，奏改冊文，非典故也。）〉
units.en: From the August and Illustrious up to Emperor Xuanzong are fourteen generations; memorializing a change to the writ text is not according to precedent.)〉
units.literal: Now from the August and Illustrious up to Emperor Xuanzong are fourteen generations; to memorialize changing the writ text is not according to precedent.)〉

units.zh: 伏詳本朝列聖之舊典，明皇定禮之新規，開元十年，特立九廟，子孫遵守，歷代無虧。
units.en: We have examined the old statutes of our dynasty's successive emperors and the new ritual regulations established under Emperor Ming; in Kaiyuan 10 nine temples were specially established, and descendants have observed this through the generations without lapse.
units.literal: Your subjects have examined in detail the old statutes of the successive sage emperors of this dynasty and the new regulations for fixing ritual under Emperor Ming; in the tenth year of Kaiyuan nine temples were specially established, observed by descendants through the generations without impairment.

units.zh: 唐初悉用祝版，唯陵廟用玉冊，玄皇親祭郊廟，用玉為冊。
units.en: Early Tang used prayer boards exclusively; only imperial tombs and temples used jade tablets, and when the August Sovereign personally sacrificed at suburban altars and temples, jade tablets were employed.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tang all used prayer boards; only imperial tombs and temples used jade tablets, and when the August Sovereign personally sacrificed at suburban altars and temples, jade was used for tablets.

units.zh: 聖朝中興，重修宗廟，今太廟見饗高祖、太宗、懿宗、昭宗、獻祖、太祖、莊宗七廟，太祖景皇帝在祧廟之數，不列廟饗。
units.en: After the dynasty's revival the ancestral shrines were rebuilt; the Imperial Temple now served seven halls—the High Ancestor, Great Ancestor, Yizong, Zhaozong, Xianzu, Taizu, and Zhuangzong—while Grand Ancestor Emperor Jing was relegated to the distant-lineage shrine and no longer received regular temple offerings.
units.literal: When the sacred court restored the dynasty and rebuilt the ancestral temples, the Imperial Ancestral Temple now offers sacrifices to seven temples: the High Ancestor, Great Ancestor, Yizong, Zhaozong, Xianzu, Taizu, and Zhuangzong. The Grand Ancestor Emperor Jing is counted among the distant ancestral temples and is not listed for temple sacrifice.

units.zh: 如或以玉難辦，寧小其制度，以取其真。」
units.en: If jade is hard to obtain, it is better to reduce the prescribed dimensions than sacrifice authenticity."
units.literal: If jade is difficult to obtain, it is better to reduce the scale of the regulations so as to preserve authenticity."

units.zh: 至如國朝，太祖曰景皇帝，以受命而有唐室，宣宗皇帝以隔代承運，皇綱復振故也。
units.en: In our dynasty, the Grand Ancestor is called Emperor Jing because he received the Mandate and possessed the Tang house; Emperor Xuanzong because he received the fortune across generations and restored the imperial norm.
units.literal: As for our dynasty, the Grand Ancestor is called Emperor Jing because he received the Mandate and possessed the Tang house; Emperor Xuanzong because he received the fortune across generations and the imperial norm was restored.

units.zh: 其後王涯判二使，置榷茶使，徙民茶樹於官場，焚其舊積者，天下大怨。
units.en: Later Wang Ya headed both commissions, created a Tea Monopoly Commissioner, transplanted private tea trees to government plantations, and burned existing stockpiles—provoking widespread outrage.
units.literal: Afterward Wang Ya judged the two commissions, set up a Tea Monopoly Commissioner, moved the people's tea trees to government fields, and burned their old stores; all under Heaven greatly resented it.

units.zh: 令狐楚代為鹽鐵使兼榷茶使，復令納榷，加價而已。
units.en: Linghu Chu succeeded him as Salt and Iron Commissioner and also Tea Monopoly Commissioner, restoring monopoly payments with price increases only.
units.literal: Linghu Chu replaced him as Salt and Iron Commissioner and also Tea Monopoly Commissioner, restoring payment of monopoly dues with price increase only.

units.zh: 八年，河東錫錢復起，鹽鐵使王涯置飛狐鑄錢院於蔚州，天下歲鑄錢不及十萬緡。
units.en: In the eighth year Hedong tin coin returned; Wang Ya established the Feihu mint at Weizhou; annual nationwide output fell below one hundred thousand strings.
units.literal: In the eighth year Hedong tin coin arose again; Salt Commissioner Wang Ya set up the Feihu mint at Weizhou; yearly casting under Heaven did not reach one hundred thousand strings.

units.zh: 子知溫、知至，悉以進士第入官。
units.en: Sons Zhiwen and Zhizhi entered service by jinshi.
units.literal: Sons Zhiwen and Zhizhi all entered office through the jinshi.

units.zh: 知至為宰相劉瞻所善，以比部郎中知制誥。
units.en: Zhizhi, cherished by Liu Zhan, became Drafting Drafter from Revenue Director.
units.literal: Zhizhi was favored by Chancellor Liu Zhan, made Drafting Drafter from Director in the Ministry of Revenue.

units.zh: 上元元年，天后上表曰：「至如父在為母服止一期，雖心喪三年，服由尊降。
units.en: In the first year of Shangyuan, Empress Wu submitted a memorial, saying: "As for when the father is alive, mourning for the mother stops at one cycle—though heart mourning is three years, the garment is reduced by reverence for the father.
units.literal: In the first year of Shangyuan, Empress Wu submitted a memorial, saying: "As for when the father is alive, mourning for the mother stops at one cycle—though heart mourning is three years, the garment is reduced by reverence for the father.

units.zh: 則天皇后請同父沒之服，三年然始除靈。
units.en: Empress Wu had asked for the same garment as when the father was dead—three years before tablet removal.
units.literal: Empress Wu Zetian requested mourning the same as when the father is dead—three years before removal of the spirit tablet.

units.zh: 高宗下詔，依議行焉，
units.en: Gaozong decreed and put her proposal into practice.
units.literal: Gaozong issued a decree and followed the proposal in practice,

units.zh: 至垂拱年中，始編入格，易代之後，俗乃通行。
units.en: Only in Chuigong was it written into the code; after the dynastic shift the custom spread.
units.literal: By the Chuigong era it was first entered into the administrative code; after the change of dynasty the custom then spread in practice.

units.zh: 竊謂子之於母，慈愛特深，非母不生，非母不育。
units.en: A child owes the mother a singular depth of love: without her there is no birth, without her no rearing.
units.literal: I venture to say that in a child's relation to the mother, affection is especially deep—without the mother one is not born, without the mother one is not reared.

units.zh: 推燥居濕，咽苦吐甘，生養勞瘁，恩斯極矣！
units.en: She tended his dryness and wetness, swallowed bitterness and gave sweetness—the labor of nurture exhausts what kindness can mean.
units.literal: Tending dryness and wetness, swallowing bitterness and spitting sweetness—the toil of bearing and rearing, kindness reaches its utmost!

units.zh: 所以禽獸之情，猶知其母，三年在懷，理宜崇報。
units.en: Even beasts know their dam; three years in the womb demand a commensurate return.
units.literal: Therefore even beasts in feeling know their mother; three years in the womb—by principle one ought to honor her in return.

units.zh: 若父在為母服止一期，尊父之敬雖周，報母之慈有闕。
units.en: Stopping at one cycle while the father lived honored him fully but left the mother's kindness short.
units.literal: If when the father is alive mourning for the mother stops at one cycle, reverence for the father is complete yet requital of the mother's kindness is lacking.

units.zh: 且齊斬之制，足為差減，更令周以一期，恐傷人子之志。
units.en: Hemmed sackcloth already graded the mourning; shrinking three years to one cycle would wound a son's intent.
units.literal: Moreover the hemmed-and-cut garment system is sufficient for graduated reduction; to make one cycle suffice where three years should apply would wound the son's intent.

units.zh: 今請父在為母終三年之服。」
units.en: We now request that when the father is alive mourning for the mother run the full three years."
units.literal: We now request that when the father is alive mourning for the mother run the full three years."

units.zh: 代宗踐祚，特嘉之，召拜工部尚書。
units.en: When Emperor Daizong took the throne he singled Guozhen out for praise and summoned him to court as minister of works.
units.literal: When Daizong ascended the throne he especially commended him and summoned him to court as Minister of Works.

units.zh: 代宗聞其事，悼惜久之。
units.en: When Daizong heard the news, he grieved for him a long while.
units.literal: When Daizong heard, he mourned him a long while.

units.zh: 大歷五年四月，會月給糧儲，兵馬使臧玠與判官達奚覯忿爭，覯曰：「今幸無事。」
units.en: In the fourth month of 770, at the monthly distribution of grain stores, army commissioner Zang Zhi quarreled with legal aide Daxi Gun. Gun said, "For the moment all is well."
units.literal: In the fourth month of the fifth year of Dali, at the monthly issue of grain stores, the army commissioner Zang Zhi quarreled with the legal aide Daxi Gun. Gun said, "For now there is nothing amiss."

units.zh: 于時，討蔡數不利，群臣爭請罷兵，錢徽、蕭俛尤確苦。
units.en: The campaign against Cai had met repeated setbacks, and ministers clamored to withdraw the armies, Qian Hui and Xiao Fu being the most insistent.
units.literal: At that time the campaign against Cai had several times been unfavorable; the ministers all vied to request stopping the army, Qian Hui and Xiao Fu being especially firm and bitter.

units.zh: 太宗因修禮官奏事之次，言及喪服，太宗曰：「又舅之與姨，親疏相似，而服紀有殊，理未為得。宜集學者詳議。餘有親重而服輕者，亦附奏聞。」於是侍中魏徵、禮部侍郎令狐德棻等奏議曰：臣聞禮所以決嫌疑，定猶豫，別同異，明是非者也。非從天降，非從地出，人情而已矣。夫親族有九，服術有六，隨恩以薄厚，稱情以立文。然舅之與姨，雖為同氣，論情度義，先後實殊。何則？舅為母之本族，姨乃外戚他族，求之母族，姨不在焉，考之經典，舅誠為重。故周王念齊，每稱舅甥之國；秦伯懷晉，實切《渭陽》之詩。在舅服止一時，為姨居喪五月，循名喪實，逐末棄本。蓋古人之情，或有未達，所宜損益，實在茲乎！《記》曰：「兄弟之子，猶子也。蓋引而進之也；嫂叔之不服，蓋推而遠之也。」禮：繼父同居，則為之期；未嘗同居，則不為服。從母之夫，舅之妻，二夫人相為服。或曰，同爨緦。然則繼父之徒，並非骨肉，服重由乎同爨，恩輕在乎異居。故知制服雖繫於名；亦緣恩之厚薄者也。或有長年之嫂，遇孩童之叔，劬勞鞠養，情若新生，分飢共寒，契闊偕老。譬同居之繼父，方他人之同爨，情義之深淺，寧可同日而言哉！在其生也，愛之同於骨肉；及其死也，則曰推而遠之。求之本原，深所未諭。若推而遠之為是，則不可生而共居；生而共居之為是，則不可死同行路。重其生而輕其死，厚其始而薄其終，稱情立文，其義安在？且事嫂見稱，載籍非一。鄭仲虞則恩禮甚篤，顏弘都則竭誠致感，馬援則見之必冠，孔伋則哭之為位。此並躬踐教義，仁深孝友，察其所尚之旨，豈非先覺者歟？但於其時，上無哲王，禮非下之所議，遂使深情郁乎千載，至理藏於萬古，其來久矣，豈不惜哉！今屬欽明在辰，聖人有作，五禮詳洽，一物無遺。猶且永念慎終，凝神遐想。以為尊卑之敘，雖煥乎大備；喪紀之制，或情理未周。爰命秩宗，更詳考正。臣等奏遵明旨，觸類旁求，採摭群經，討論傳記。或引兼名實，無文之禮咸秩，惇睦之情畢舉，變薄俗於既往，垂篤義於將來，信六籍所不能談，超百王而獨得者也。諸儒所守，互有異同，詳求厥中，申明聖旨。謹按曾祖父母舊服齊衰三月，請加為齊衰五月。嫡子婦舊服大功，請加為期。眾子婦小功，今請與兄弟子婦同為大功九月。嫂叔舊無服，今請服小功五月報。其弟妻及夫兄，亦小功五月。舅服緦麻，請與從母同服小功。
units.en: While Taizong was hearing the ritual-revision officers report on business, the subject reached mourning dress. Taizong said: "Also, maternal uncles and maternal aunts are similar in closeness, yet the mourning regulations differ for them; in principle this does not seem right. Scholars should be assembled to deliberate on it in detail. Other cases where kinship is heavy but mourning is light should also be appended and reported." Thereupon Palace Attendant Wei Zheng, Vice Minister of Rites Linghu Defen, and others memorialized in deliberation: Your servants have heard that ritual is what resolves doubts and suspicions, settles hesitations, distinguishes sameness and difference, and clarifies right and wrong. It does not descend from Heaven or emerge from earth; it is simply human feeling. Kin have nine degrees and mourning techniques have six, thinning or thickening according to affection and establishing the text according to feeling. Yet although maternal uncle and maternal aunt are of the same breath, when feeling is discussed and obligation measured, the former and latter are truly different. Why? The maternal uncle belongs to the mother's root clan, while the maternal aunt is an external relative of another clan. Seeking within the mother's clan, the maternal aunt is not there; examining the classics, the maternal uncle is truly weighty. Therefore when the Zhou king remembered Qi, he always called it the state of uncle and nephew; when the Earl of Qin cherished Jin, it was truly close to the poem Weiyang. For a maternal uncle, mourning stops at one season; for a maternal aunt, one mourns five months. This follows the name and loses the substance, pursuing the branch and abandoning the root. The feeling of the ancients perhaps had something not yet fully reached, and what should be reduced or increased truly lies here. The Record says: "The sons of brothers are like sons; this draws them in and advances them. That elder-brother's wife and younger-brother-in-law do not mourn each other pushes them away." In ritual, for a stepfather who has lived with one, one wears one-year mourning; if he has never lived with one, one wears no mourning. A mother's sister's husband and a maternal uncle's wife, these two spouses mourn one another. Some say that those who share the cooking hearth wear fine hemp. Thus stepfathers and such are not flesh and blood, yet mourning is heavy because of sharing the hearth, and affection is light because of living apart. Therefore we know that although mourning dress depends on names, it also follows the thickness or thinness of affection. Sometimes there is an elder sister-in-law of advanced years with a younger brother-in-law who was a child; she toiled to raise him, with feeling as if newly giving birth, sharing hunger and cold, and staying with him through hardship into old age. Compared with a stepfather who shared the household or with another person sharing the cooking hearth, how could the depth or shallowness of feeling and obligation be discussed on the same day? While she lives, he loves her as flesh and blood; when she dies, one says she is pushed away. Seeking the root of this, we deeply fail to understand it. If pushing away is right, then they should not live together while alive. If living together while alive is right, then they cannot be treated as people on the road when dead. To value the living and slight the dead, to thicken the beginning and thin the end: where is the meaning of matching feeling and establishing text? Moreover, serving a sister-in-law is praised in more than one written record. Zheng Zhongyu's grace and ritual were very deep; Yan Hongdu exhausted sincerity and produced a response; Ma Yuan always put on his cap when seeing his sister-in-law; Kong Ji cried for his sister-in-law with a set position. These all personally practiced teaching and obligation, with benevolence deep in filial and fraternal feeling. Examining the purpose of what they honored, were they not those who awakened first? Only in their time there was no wise king above, and ritual was not for those below to debate; thus deep feeling was suppressed for a thousand years, and perfect principle was hidden for ten thousand ages. This has been so for a long time; is it not regrettable? Now we meet a time when reverent brightness is present and a sage has arisen. The five rites are detailed and complete, with not one thing omitted. Still Your Majesty forever thinks on careful endings and concentrates spirit in distant reflection, considering that although the sequence of honored and lowly is bright and fully prepared, the regulations of mourning may not yet be complete in feeling and principle. Therefore you ordered the Minister of Rites to examine and correct them in more detail. Your servants, in memorializing, follow the bright command, seek sideways by analogy, gather from the many classics, and discuss commentaries and records. Some cases draw on both name and substance; rites without written text are all ordered, and the feeling of generous harmony is fully raised, changing thin customs from the past and transmitting deep obligation to the future. This is truly what the six classics could not discuss and what surpasses the hundred kings as Your Majesty's sole attainment. The various scholars hold to different views. We have sought the center in detail and extend and clarify the sage command. Respectfully, the old mourning for great-grandparents was three months of trimmed mourning; we request increasing it to five months of trimmed mourning. The old mourning for the principal son's wife was great-work mourning; we request increasing it to one year. The mourning for wives of other sons was small-work mourning; we now request making it the same as for brothers' sons' wives, great-work mourning for nine months. Elder-brother's wife and younger-brother-in-law formerly had no mourning; we now request reciprocal small-work mourning for five months. The younger brother's wife and her husband's elder brother should also have small-work mourning for five months. Mourning for a maternal uncle was fine hemp; we request making it the same as for a mother's sister, small-work mourning.

Respectfully, the old mourning for great-grandparents was three months of trimmed mourning; we request increasing it to five months of trimmed mourning. The old mourning for the principal son's wife was great-work mourning; we request increasing it to one year. The mourning for wives of other sons was small-work mourning; we now request making it the same as for brothers' sons' wives, great-work mourning for nine months. Elder-brother's wife and younger-brother-in-law formerly had no mourning; we now request reciprocal small-work mourning for five months. The younger brother's wife and her husband's elder brother should also have small-work mourning for five months. Mourning for a maternal uncle was fine hemp; we request making it the same as for a mother's sister, small-work mourning.

units.zh: 貞觀年中，八座議奏：『舅服同姨，小功五月。』
units.en: In Zhenguan the Eight Seats had ruled that mourning for a mother's brother matched that for a mother's sister: five months' lesser accomplishment.
units.literal: In the Zhenguan era the Eight Seats deliberated and memorialized: 'For the mother's brother, mourning is the same as for the mother's sister—five months' lesser accomplishment.

units.zh: 刑部郎中田再思建議曰：干尊坤卑，天一地二，陰陽之位分矣，夫婦之道配焉。至若死喪之威，隆殺之等，禮經五服之制，齊斬有殊，考妣三年之喪，貴賤無隔，以報免懷之慈，以酬罔極之恩者也。稽之上古，喪期無數，暨乎中葉，方有歲年。《禮》云：「五帝殊時，不相沿樂；三王異代，不相襲禮。」《白虎通》云：「質文再變，正朔三而復。」自周公制禮之後，孔父刊經已來，爰殊厭降之儀，以標服紀之節。重輕從俗，斟酌隨時。故知禮不從天而降，不由地而出也，在人消息，為適時之中耳。春秋諸國，魯最知禮，以周公之後，孔子之邦也。晉韓起來聘，言「周禮盡在魯矣。」齊仲孫來盟，言「魯猶秉周禮。」尚有子張問高宗諒陰三年，子思不聽其子服出母，子游謂同母異父昆弟之服大功，子夏謂合從齊衰之制。此等並四科之數，十哲之人，高步孔門，親承聖訓，及遇喪事，猶此致疑，即明自古已來，升降不一者也。三年之制，說者紛然。鄭玄以為二十七月，王肅以為二十五月。又改葬之服，鄭云服緦三月，王云訖葬而除。又繼母出嫁，鄭云皆服，王云從於繼育，乃為之服。又無服之殤，鄭云子生一月，哭之一日；王云以哭之一日易服之月。鄭、王祖經宗傳，各有異同；荀摯采古求遺，互為損益。方知去聖漸遠，殘缺彌多。故曰會禮之家，名為聚訟，寧有定哉！而父在為母三年，行之已逾四紀，出自高宗大帝之代，不從則天皇后之朝。大帝御極之辰，中宮獻書之日，往時參議，將可施行，編之於格，服之已久。前王所是，疏而為律；後王所是，著而為令。何必乖先帝之旨，阻人子之情，虧純孝之心，背德義之本？有何妨於聖化，有何紊於彝倫，而欲服之週年，與伯叔母齊焉，與姑姊妹同焉？夫三年之喪，如白駒之過隙，君子喪親，有終身之憂，何況再周乎！夫禮者，體也，履也，示之以跡。孝者，畜也，養也，因之以心。小人不恥不仁，不畏不義。服之有制，使愚人企及；衣之以衰，使見之摧痛。以此防人，人猶有朝死而夕忘者；以此制人，人猶有釋服而從吉者。方今漸歸古樸，須敦孝義，抑賢引愚，理資寧戚，食稻衣錦，所不忍聞。若以庶事朝儀，一依周禮，則古之人臣見君也，公卿大夫贄羔雁、珪璧，今何故不依乎？周之用刑也，墨、劓、宮、刖，今何故不行乎？周則侯、甸、男、衛，朝聘有數，今何故不行乎？周則不五十不仕，七十不入朝，今何故不依乎？周則井、邑、丘、甸，以立徵稅，今何故不行乎？周則三老五等，父死子及，今何故不行乎？周則冠冕衣裘，乘車而戰，今何故不行乎？周則分土五更，膠序養老，今何故不行乎？諸如此例，不可勝述。何獨孝思之事，愛一年之服於其母乎？可為痛心，可為慟哭者！《詩》云：「哀哀父母，生我劬勞。」《禮》云：「父之親子也，親賢而下無能；母之親子也，賢則親之，無能則憐之。」阮嗣宗晉代之英才，方外之高士，以為母重於父。據齊斬升數，粗細已降，何忍服之節制，減至於周？豈後代之士，盡慚於古。循古未必是，依今未必非也。又同爨服緦，禮經明義。嫂叔遠別，同諸路人。引而進之，觸類而長。猶子咸衣苴枲，季父不服緦麻，推遠之情有餘，睦親之義未足。又母之昆弟，情切渭陽，翟酺訟舅之冤，甯氏宅甥之相，我之出也，義亦殷焉。不同從母之尊，遂降小功之服，依諸古禮，有爽俗情。今貶舅而宗姨，是陋今而榮古。此並太宗之制也，行之百年矣，輒為刊復，實用有疑。
units.en: Tian Zaisi, Bureau Director in the Ministry of Justice, made a proposal: Qian is honored and kun is lowly; Heaven is one and earth is two. The positions of yin and yang are divided, and the way of husband and wife is paired with them. As for the awe of death and mourning and the grades of fullness and reduction, the ritual classics have the system of the five mourning grades. Trimmed and unhemmed mourning differ, but the three-year mourning for father and mother has no barrier between noble and base, because it repays the kindness of bearing and cherishing and answers boundless grace. Examining high antiquity, mourning terms had no fixed number; by middle antiquity, only then were there years and months. The Ritual says: "The Five Emperors differed in time and did not follow one another in music; the Three Kings differed in age and did not inherit one another's rites." The Baihu Tong says: "Plainness and refinement change twice, and the first month changes through three and returns." Since the Duke of Zhou made ritual and since Confucius edited the classics, there have been different rules of suppression and reduction to mark the divisions of mourning regulations. Heavy and light follow custom; deliberation and adjustment follow the time. Thus we know ritual does not descend from Heaven or come out from earth; it lies in human increase and decrease, making what fits the time and the mean. Among the states of the Spring and Autumn, Lu best knew ritual, because it was the descendants of the Duke of Zhou and the state of Confucius. When Han Qi of Jin came on a visit, he said, "The rites of Zhou are all in Lu." When Zhongsun of Qi came to make a covenant, he said, "Lu still holds the rites of Zhou." Yet Zizhang asked about Gaozong's three years of silent mourning; Zisi did not allow his son to wear mourning for his divorced mother; Ziyou said that brothers with the same mother but different fathers should wear great-work mourning; Zixia said they should follow the trimmed-mourning rule. These were all among the numbered disciples of the four categories and the ten philosophers, men of high rank in Confucius's gate who personally received the sage teaching; yet when they encountered mourning matters, they still produced doubts like this. This makes clear that since antiquity increases and reductions have not been uniform. As for the three-year system, explanations are confused. Zheng Xuan considered it twenty-seven months; Wang Su considered it twenty-five months. Again for mourning after reburial, Zheng says one wears fine hemp for three months, while Wang says one removes it when burial is completed. Again for a stepmother who remarries, Zheng says all wear mourning, while Wang says that only if one followed and was raised by her does one wear mourning. Again for a child who died young and for whom there is no mourning, Zheng says that for a child born one month, one cries one day; Wang says one day of crying replaces one month of mourning. Zheng and Wang each take the classics as ancestor and the commentaries as lineage, and each has differences. Xun Zhi collected antiquity and sought what was left, alternately reducing and increasing. From this we know that as the sages recede farther away, gaps and losses become more numerous. Therefore it is said that houses that assemble ritual are called gathered lawsuits; how could there be a fixed answer? Yet the three-year mourning for a mother while the father is alive has been practiced for more than forty years. It came from the generation of Gaozong the Great Emperor, not from the court of Empress Zetian. When the Great Emperor ruled and the palace submitted the document, the former deliberations could be put into practice; it was compiled into the regulations, and the mourning has been worn for a long time. What a former king approved was set out as law; what a later king approved was written as ordinance. Why must we oppose the former emperor's intent, block the feeling of a person's son, diminish a pure filial heart, and turn against the root of virtue and obligation? What harm is there to sage transformation? What disorder is there to the constant human order, that one would make the mourning one year, equal to that for paternal uncles' wives, and the same as for paternal aunts and sisters? The three-year mourning passes like a white colt through a crack; a gentleman mourning his parent has lifelong grief, how much more for two full cycles! Ritual is embodiment, practice, showing it by traces. Filial piety is storing up, nourishing, following it by the heart. Petty people are not ashamed of inhumanity and do not fear unrighteousness. Mourning dress has regulations to make foolish people reach upward; they are clothed in mourning garments so that seeing them produces crushing pain. Using this to guard people, there are still those who forget by evening one who died in the morning. Using this to regulate people, there are still those who remove mourning and follow auspicious affairs. Now we are gradually returning to ancient simplicity and must deepen filial piety and obligation. Restraining the worthy and drawing in the foolish, in principle, depends on Ning Qi; eating rice and wearing brocade are things one cannot bear to hear. If ordinary affairs and court ceremony are all to follow the Zhou rites, then when ancient ministers saw the ruler, dukes, ministers, and great officers presented lambs, geese, jade tablets, and disks; why do we not follow this now? Zhou punishments used tattooing, nose-cutting, castration, and foot-cutting; why do we not carry them out now? Zhou had hou, dian, nan, and wei domains, and audiences and visits had fixed numbers; why do we not carry this out now? Zhou did not let one serve before fifty, and at seventy one did not enter court; why do we not follow this now? Zhou used jing, yi, qiu, and dian to establish taxation; why do we not carry this out now? Zhou had three elders and five grades, father dying and son succeeding; why do we not carry this out now? Zhou used caps, robes, fur garments, and chariots in battle; why do we not carry this out now? Zhou divided land and had five geng, and in village and school nourished the aged; why do we not carry this out now? Examples such as these cannot be fully stated. Why only in the matter of filial thought begrudge one year of mourning for one's mother? This can make the heart ache; this can make one wail. The Odes says: "Alas, alas, my father and mother, who bore me with toil." The Ritual says: "When a father loves his child, he loves the worthy and lowers the incapable; when a mother loves her child, if worthy she loves him, and if incapable she pities him." Ruan Sizong, an outstanding talent of Jin and lofty man beyond the world, considered the mother weightier than the father. Based on the thread counts of trimmed and unhemmed mourning, coarseness and fineness already descend. How can one bear for the term of mourning to be reduced to one year? Surely later men are not all ashamed before antiquity. Following antiquity is not necessarily right; following the present is not necessarily wrong. Again, those who share the cooking hearth wear fine hemp; this is a clear meaning of the ritual classics. Elder-brother's wife and younger-brother-in-law are kept distant and treated like people on the road. Drawing them in and advancing them extends by analogy. Nephews all wear hemp mourning, but a younger uncle does not wear fine hemp; the feeling of pushing away is more than enough, and the obligation of harmonizing kin is insufficient. Again the mother's brothers have feeling as close as Weiyang; Di Pu litigated his uncle's injustice, and the Ning family housed a nephew as minister. Since I come from them, obligation too is deep. Not sharing the honor of a mother's sister, they are thereby lowered to small-work mourning. According to the ancient rites, this conflicts with common feeling. Now lowering the maternal uncle while honoring the maternal aunt is to scorn the present and glorify antiquity. These are all Taizong's regulations and have been practiced for a hundred years; rashly cutting and restoring them truly creates doubt.

units.zh: 制可之。
units.en: The throne approved.
units.literal: The ordinance approved it.

units.zh: 時王起選士三十人，而楊知至、竇緘、源重、鄭樸及嚴五人皆世胄，起以聞，詔獨收嚴。
units.en: Wang Qi then selected thirty candidates; Yang Zhizhi, Dou Jian, Yuan Chong, Zheng Pu, and Yan—five men from eminent houses—were among them; Qi reported this, and an edict ordered Yan alone accepted.
units.literal: At the time Wang Qi selected thirty candidates, and Yang Zhizhi, Dou Jian, Yuan Chong, Zheng Pu, and Yan—five men—were all from eminent houses; Qi reported this, and an edict ordered that Yan alone be accepted.

units.zh: 宣宗追加順、憲二宗尊號，有司議改造廟主，署新謚，詔百官議。
units.en: When Emperor Xuanzong added posthumous honorific titles for Emperors Shun and Xian, the relevant offices debated remaking temple tablets and affixing new posthumous designations, and an edict ordered all officials to discuss it.
units.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong added posthumous honorific titles for Emperors Shun and Xian, the relevant offices debated remaking the temple tablets and affixing new posthumous designations, and an edict ordered all officials to discuss it.

units.zh: 蓋唐室自懿宗失政，天下亂離，故武宗以下實錄，不傳於世。
units.en: From Tang Yizong's loss of rule the realm shattered; veritable records from Wuzong down no longer circulated.
units.literal: It is that from Emperor Yizong of Tang the government was lost and the realm torn apart; therefore veritable records from Emperor Wuzong down were not transmitted in the world.

units.zh: 王承元徙義成軍，遣諫議大夫鄭覃往慰成德軍，賚緡錢百萬。
units.en: Wang Chengyuan was shifted to Yicheng; Remonstrator Zheng Tan was sent to comfort Chengde with a million strings of cash.
units.literal: When Wang Chengyuan was moved to the Yicheng army, Remonstrator of the Left Zheng Tan was sent to comfort the Chengde army, bearing a million strings of cash.

units.zh: 楊虞卿，字師臯，虢州弘農人。
units.en: Yang Yuqing, style name Shigao, came from Hongnong in Guo.
units.literal: Yang Yuqing, styled Shigao, was a native of Hongnong in Guo Prefecture.

units.zh: 宗閔待之尤厚，就黨中為最能唱和者，以口語軒輊事機，故時號「黨魁」。
units.en: Zongmin favored him most; in the clique he led the chorus and steered affairs by rumor, earning the title "Faction Chief."
units.literal: Zongmin treated him especially well; among the faction he was the best at echoing and harmonizing, weighing affairs by gossip, hence the nickname "Faction Chief."

units.zh: 虞卿第進士、博學宏辭，為校書郎。
units.en: Yuqing took jinshi and erudite macrocosmic degrees and served as collator.
units.literal: Yuqing passed the jinshi and the erudite macrocosmic examination and served as collator.

units.zh: 還，遷侍御史，改禮部員外郎、史館脩撰。
units.en: Returning, he became Attending Censor, then Vice Director of Rites and Historiography compiler.
units.literal: On return he was made Attending Censor, then Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites and compiler in the Historiography Institute.

units.zh: 李宗閔、牛僧孺輔政，引為右司郎中、弘文館學士。
units.en: Under Li Zongmin and Niu Sengru he became Right Department Director and Hongwen academician.
units.literal: When Li Zongmin and Niu Sengru held government, they brought him in as Right Department Director and Erudite of the Hongwen Institute.

units.zh: 宗閔復入，以工部侍郎召，遷京兆尹。
units.en: Zongmin's return brought him back as Vice Minister of Works and Jingzhao magistrate.
units.literal: When Zongmin returned to power, he was summoned as Vice Minister of Works and made metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao.

units.zh: 當時有蘇景胤、張元夫，而虞卿兄弟汝士、漢公為人所奔向，故語曰：「欲趨舉場，問蘇、張；
units.en: Su Jingyin and Zhang Yuanfu still mattered, but Yuqing's brothers Rushi and Hangong drew the crowds, so people said: "For the examination field, ask Su and Zhang;
units.literal: At the time there were Su Jingyin and Zhang Yuanfu, but Yuqing's brothers Rushi and Hangong were where men rushed, hence the saying: "If you wish to hurry to the examination ground, ask Su and Zhang;

units.zh: 子知退、知權、壇、堪、漢公，皆擢進士第，漢公最顯。
units.en: Sons Zhitui, Zhiquan, Tan, Kan, and Hangong all took the jinshi; Hangong shone brightest.
units.literal: Sons Zhituo, Zhiquan, Tan, Kan, and Hangong all passed the jinshi; Hangong was most prominent.

units.zh: 穆宗初立，逸遊荒恣，虞卿上疏曰：「烏鳶遭害仁鳥逝，誹謗不誅良臣進。
units.en: At Muzong's accession, given to idle roaming and dissipation, Yuqing submitted: "When carrion birds are harmed, the virtuous birds flee; when calumny goes unpunished, good ministers come forward.
units.literal: When Emperor Muzong first took the throne, indulging in roaming pleasures and reckless abandon, Yuqing memorialized: "When crows and kites suffer harm the benevolent birds depart; when slander is not punished worthy ministers advance.

units.zh: 臣敢冒誅獻瞽言。
units.en: I dare risk death to offer my humble counsel.
units.literal: Your servant dares risk execution to offer blind counsel.

units.zh: 臣聞堯、舜以天下為憂，不以位為樂。
units.en: I have heard that Yao and Shun worried for the realm rather than rejoiced in their rank.
units.literal: Your servant has heard that Yao and Shun took the empire's cares as their own and did not treat the throne as pleasure.

units.zh: 況今北虜方梗，西戎弗靖，兩河有瘡痏之虞，五嶺罹氛厲之役。
units.en: The northern enemy blocks the frontier, the western tribes are unquiet, the two He circuits bear festering troubles, and the Five Ridges labor under plague and levy.
units.literal: Moreover, the northern barbarians are now obstructive, the western tribes unsettled, the two He regions face the peril of running sores, and the Five Ridges suffer pestilence and corvée.

units.zh: 人之疾苦積下，朝之制度莫脩。
units.en: Popular hardship piles up below, yet court institutions go unmended.
units.literal: The people's suffering accumulates below, while the court's institutions are not repaired.

units.zh: 邊亡見儲，國用浸屈，固未可以高枕而息也。
units.en: Border granaries stand empty and the treasury shrinks; one cannot pillow one's head high and sleep in peace.
units.literal: The borders show empty stores, state revenue daily contracts—truly one cannot rest high on a pillow and be at ease.

units.zh: 陛下初臨萬幾，宜有憂天下心。
units.en: Your Majesty has only just taken the myriad reins; you should bear the empire in mind.
units.literal: Your Majesty has newly assumed the myriad affairs; you ought to have a heart that worries for the empire.

units.zh: 當日見輔臣公卿百執事，垂意以問，使四方內外灼有所聞。
units.en: Meet your chief ministers, nobles, and the hundred officers daily, question them with care, and let the realm see it plainly.
units.literal: Each day you should receive chief ministers, dukes, and the hundred officials, showing concern in inquiry, so that within and without all clearly hear.

units.zh: 而聽政六十日，入對延英，獨三數大臣承聖問而已，它內朝臣偕入齊出，無所咨詢。
units.en: Yet in sixty days at court, at Yanying audiences only a few senior ministers heard your questions; the rest of the inner officials filed in and out with no counsel sought.
units.literal: Yet in sixty days of hearing government, entering audience at Yanying, only three or four great ministers received the sacred inquiry; other inner-court officials entered and left together with no consultation.

units.zh: 諫臣盈廷，忠言不聞，臣實羞之。
units.en: The remonstrators crowd the hall yet loyal speech never reaches you—I am ashamed of it.
units.literal: Remonstrators fill the hall yet loyal words are not heard—I am truly ashamed.

units.zh: 蓋主恩疏而正路塞也。
units.en: Imperial grace has grown remote and the straight road is blocked.
units.literal: This is because imperial favor is distant and the upright path blocked.

units.zh: 公卿大臣宜朝夕燕見，則君臣情接而治道得矣。
units.en: High ministers should meet you morning and evening in relaxed audience, so feeling joins between ruler and servant and governance is secured.
units.literal: Dukes and great ministers ought to be received morning and evening in easy audience, so that ruler and minister join in feeling and the way of rule is attained.

units.zh: 今宰臣四五人，或頃刻侍坐，鞠躬隕越，隨旨上下，無能往來，此繇君太尊、臣太卑故也。
units.en: Today four or five chancellors may sit a moment, bowing until they nearly fall, bobbing at your nod, unable to speak freely—because the throne is too lofty and the servants too abject.
units.literal: Now four or five chief ministers sometimes sit for a moment, bowing with bodies bent low, rising and falling at the imperial will, unable to exchange words—this is because the lord is too exalted and the servants too low.

units.zh: 公卿列位，雖陟降清地，曾未奉優眷、承下問。
units.en: The ranked nobles, though raised to exalted posts, have never tasted your gracious notice or your questioning ear.
units.literal: The ranks of dukes, though promoted to pure posts, have never received gracious favor or answered inquiry from below.

units.zh: 雖陛下神聖如五帝，猶宜周爰顧逮，惠以氣色，使支體相成，君臣昭明。
units.en: Even if you are as sage as the Five Emperors, you should still look widely, show a warm face, and knit trunk and limbs so ruler and minister shine upon each other.
units.literal: Though Your Majesty is as sagely as the Five Emperors, you should still look about with care, show a kindly countenance, and make limbs and trunk work together so ruler and minister are bright to each other.

units.zh: 陛下求治於宰相，宰相求治於臣等，進忠若趨利，論政若訴冤，此而不治，無有也。
units.en: You seek order from the chancellor, the chancellor from us; if loyalty is pursued like profit and policy debated like a grievance, nothing will remain ungoverned.
units.literal: Your Majesty seeks good rule from the chancellor; the chancellor seeks good rule from us; if advancing loyalty is like rushing profit and discussing government like pleading wrongs, with this there will be no failure to govern.

units.zh: 自古天子居危思安之心同，而居安慮危之心則異，故不得皆為聖明也。」
units.en: In danger all rulers think of safety alike, but in safety their thoughts of peril differ—so not every throne is sage."
units.literal: From antiquity the hearts of sons of Heaven in peril thinking of safety are the same, but in safety thinking of peril they differ—hence not all can be sage and bright."

units.zh: 會曹史李賨等鬻偽告，調官六十五員，贓千六百萬以上，虞卿發其奸，賨等系御史府。
units.en: Clerks led by Li Bin sold forged appointment notices for sixty-five posts, taking more than sixteen million in bribes; Yuqing exposed them and they were jailed in the censorate.
units.literal: When clerks Li Bin and others sold false appointment notices, adjusting sixty-five offices, with bribes above sixteen million, Yuqing exposed the fraud and Bin and the rest were held in the censorate prison.

units.zh: 帝大怒，下虞卿詔獄。
units.en: The emperor flew into a rage and imprisoned Yuqing.
units.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and sent Yuqing to the imperial prison.

units.zh: 於是諸子弟自囚闕下稱冤，虞卿得釋，貶虔州司戶參軍，死。
units.en: His sons and brothers then chained themselves at the palace gate pleading injustice; he was freed, demoted to Qianzhou army aide, and died.
units.literal: Then the sons and brothers imprisoned themselves below the palace gate crying injustice; Yuqing was released, demoted to Qianzhou army aide, and died.

units.zh: 虞卿佞柔，善諧麗權幸，倚為奸利。
units.en: Yuqing was pliant and flattering, adept at charming favorites, and traded on them for corrupt profit.
units.literal: Yuqing was fawning and supple, skilled at pleasing the powerful with witty grace, relying on them for illicit gain.

units.zh: 太和九年，京師訛言鄭註為帝治丹，剔小兒肝心用之。
units.en: In Taihe year nine the capital rumored that Zheng Zhu brewed elixir for the emperor by cutting out children's livers and hearts.
units.literal: In the ninth year of Taihe, the capital rumor said Zheng Zhu was making elixir for the emperor, gouging out small boys' livers and hearts for use.

units.zh: 溫固執，文宗諭而止。
units.en: Wei held firm until Wenzong instructed him to stop.
units.literal: Wei persisted; Emperor Wenzong instructed him and he desisted.

units.zh: 開成初，文宗欲以真源、臨真二公主降士族，謂宰相曰：「民間脩婚姻，不計官品而上閥閱。
units.en: Early in Kaicheng, Wenzong meant to marry the Princesses Zhenyuan and Linzhen into great clans and told his chief ministers: "Common folk arranging marriages care nothing for office and everything for pedigree.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Kaicheng era, Emperor Wenzong wished to marry the Princesses Zhenyuan and Linzhen to gentry families and said to the chief ministers: "Among the people in arranging marriages, they do not consider official rank but esteem clan pedigree.

units.zh: 乃以戶部侍郎趙贊判度支，代佑行借錢令，約罷兵乃償之。
units.en: Zhao Zan, vice minister of revenue, was assigned to the directorate of revenue to replace Du You and enforce the loan order, with repayment promised after the armies stood down.
units.literal: Thereupon the Vice Minister of Revenue Zhao Zan was put in charge of the Directorate of Revenue to replace You and carry out the borrowing order, with repayment promised once the troops were disbanded.

units.zh: 至是趙贊又言：「自軍興，常平倉廢垂三十年，凶荒潰散，餧死相食，不可勝紀。
units.en: Zhao Zan now argued: "Since the wars began, ever-normal granaries have been neglected for nearly thirty years. Famine drove people apart; they starved in such numbers that corpses fed the living beyond counting.
units.literal: At this time Zhao Zan again said: "Since the outbreak of war the ever-normal granaries have lain abandoned for nearly thirty years; amid famine people scattered and starved, feeding on one another in numbers beyond counting.

units.zh: 趙贊復請稅間架，算除陌。
units.en: Zhao Zan next proposed the structure tax and the transaction-stamp levy.
units.literal: Zhao Zan again requested taxation on structures and calculation of the transaction-stamp levy.

units.zh: 陛下即位，京城兩市置常平官，雖頻年少雨，米不騰貴，可推而廣之，宜兼儲布帛。
units.en: Since Your Majesty's accession, ever-normal officers in the capital's two markets have kept grain prices steady despite poor rains. The system should be expanded, and cloth and silk stockpiled as well.
units.literal: Since Your Majesty's accession, ever-normal officers have been placed in the two markets of the capital; though rain was scant in successive years, grain did not soar in price. This may be extended broadly; cloth and silk should also be stored.

units.zh: 請於兩都、江陵、成都、揚、汴、蘇、洪置常平輕重本錢，上至百萬緡，下至十萬，積米、粟、布、帛、絲、麻，貴則下價而出之，賤則加估而收之。
units.en: He proposed ever-normal funds from one million strings down to one hundred thousand at the two capitals, Jiangling, Chengdu, Yangzhou, Bian, Suzhou, and Hongzhou, stockpiling grain, cloth, silk, and hemp to sell cheap when prices rose and buy dear when they fell.
units.literal: He requested that in the two capitals, Jiangling, Chengdu, Yang, Bian, Su, and Hong, ever-normal capital be set in light and heavy amounts from one million strings down to one hundred thousand, storing rice, millet, cloth, silk, thread, and hemp; when prices were high they would sell at reduced price, when low they would buy at added valuation.

units.zh: 諸道津會置吏，閱商賈錢，每緡稅二十，竹、木、茶、漆稅十之一，以贍常平本錢。」
units.en: Tax agents at circuit crossings were to inspect merchant funds, levy twenty cash per string, and take one-tenth on bamboo, timber, tea, and lacquer to fund the ever-normal reserves."
units.literal: At ferry crossings in each circuit officers were to be placed to inspect merchants' cash, taxing twenty cash per string, and bamboo, timber, tea, and lacquer one-tenth, to support ever-normal capital."

units.zh: 舜卿，字讚聖，父敖，字碩夫，戶部尚書、渤海縣男。
units.en: Shunqing's style was Zansheng. His father Ao, style Shuofu, had been minister of revenue and Baron of Bohai County.
units.literal: Shunqing, style name Zansheng; his father Ao, style name Shuofu, was Minister of Revenue and Baron of Bohai County.

units.zh: 大和末，王起奏立營田。
units.en: Late in Dahe (835), Wang Qi memorialized to establish garrison farms.
units.literal: Late in Dahe, Wang Qi memorialized to establish garrison fields.

units.zh: 京畿觀察使李棲筠歿，代之。
units.en: When Li Qiyun, observation commissioner of the capital region, died, Han succeeded him.
units.literal: When Li Qiyun, observation commissioner of the capital region, died, Han replaced him.

units.zh: 嚴武白寧為利州刺史，既至，賊遁去，由是知名。
units.en: Yan Wu recommended Ning for prefect of Lizhou; on his arrival the bandits dispersed, and he won a name for himself.
units.literal: Yan Wu petitioned that Ning be made Administrator of Li Prefecture; once he arrived the bandits fled, and thereby he became known.

units.zh: 及武為劍南節度使，過州，心欲與俱西，而利非所屬，使寧自為計。
units.en: When Yan Wu became military governor of Jiannan and passed through Lizhou, he wanted Ning to accompany him west, but Lizhou lay outside his circuit, so he told Ning to find his own way.
units.literal: When Wu became Military Governor of Jiannan he passed through the prefecture and wished in his heart to take him west together, but Li was not under his jurisdiction, so he had Ning devise his own plan.

units.zh: 於是武遣寧將而西，既薄賊城，城皆累石，不得攻，惟東南不合者丈許，諜知之，乃為地道，再宿而拔，拓地數百里。
units.en: Yan Wu sent Ning west; the stone-walled rebel stronghold could not be stormed until spies found a one-zhang gap in the southeast; Ning dug a tunnel, took the city in two nights, and extended Tang control for hundreds of li.
units.literal: Thereupon Wu sent Ning to lead troops west; once he drew near the rebel city, the walls were all piled stone and could not be assaulted; only on the southeast was a gap of about a zhang—spies learned this, and he made a tunnel; in two nights he took it and extended territory for several hundred li.

units.zh: 及還，武大悅，裝七寶輿迎入成都，以誇於軍。
units.en: On his return Yan Wu was overjoyed, met him in Chengdu with a jeweled carriage, and paraded the honor before the army.
units.literal: When he returned, Wu was greatly pleased, fitted out a seven-jeweled carriage to welcome him into Chengdu, and displayed this to boast before the army.

units.zh: 武然之，以奇錦珍貝遺獻誠，且求寧，獻誠果喜，令自移疾去。
units.en: Yan Wu agreed, sent rare silks and jewels to Xiancheng and asked for Ning; delighted, Xiancheng let Ning resign on grounds of illness.
units.literal: Wu approved this, sent rare silks and precious shells to Xiancheng and also requested Ning; Xiancheng was indeed pleased and ordered him to remove himself on grounds of illness.

units.zh: 武遂奏為漢州刺史。
units.en: Yan Wu then had him appointed prefect of Hanzhou.
units.literal: Wu thereupon memorialized that he be made Administrator of Han Prefecture.

units.zh: 永泰元年，武卒。
units.en: In 765 Yan Wu died.
units.literal: In the first year of Yongtai, Wu died.

units.zh: 是時，第策官左散騎常侍馮宿、太常少卿賈餗、庫部郎中龐嚴見蕡對嗟伏，以為過古晁、董，而畏中官眥睚，不敢取。
units.en: At that time the examination graders — Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry Feng Su, Vice Minister of Rites Jia Su, and Bureau Director of the Storehouses Pang Yan — seeing Fen's answers sighed in admiration, holding them to surpass the ancient Chao Cuo and Dong Zhongshu; yet fearing the inner eunuchs' resentment, they dared not select him.
units.literal: At that time the examination graders — Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry Feng Su, Vice Minister of Rites Jia Su, and Bureau Director of the Storehouses Pang Yan — seeing Fen's answers sighed in admiration, holding them to surpass the ancient Chao and Dong; yet fearing the inner officials' resentful glares, they dared not select him.

units.zh: 賈餗與王涯、李訓、舒元輿位宰相，以謀敗，皆為中官夷其宗，而宦者益橫，帝以憂崩。
units.en: Jia Su with Wang Ya, Li Xun, and Shu Yuanyu held the chief ministership; when the plot failed, all were exterminated in their clans by the eunuchs — and the eunuchs grew more overbearing; the emperor died of grief.
units.literal: Jia Su with Wang Ya, Li Xun, and Shu Yuanyu held the chief ministership; when the plot failed, all were exterminated in their clans by inner officials — and the eunuchs grew more overbearing; the emperor died of grief.

units.zh: 蕡對後七年，有甘露之難。
units.en: Seven years after Fen's answers came the Sweet Dew calamity.
units.literal: Seven years after Fen's answers came the Sweet Dew calamity.

units.zh: 制又從之。
units.en: The throne approved again.
units.literal: The ordinance again approved.

units.zh: 交遊不雜，與楊綰、崔祐甫相善。
units.en: He kept his associations selective and was on good terms with Yang Wan and Cui Youfu.
units.literal: His associations were not mixed; he was on good terms with Yang Wan and Cui Youfu.

units.zh: 設使高祖再生，太宗復出，又胡為哉！
units.en: Even if Gaozu were reborn and Taizong reappeared, what could they do!
units.literal: Even if Gaozu were reborn and Taizong reappeared, what could they do!

units.zh: 仍以見素子諤及中書舍人賈至充冊禮使判官。
units.en: Jiansu's son E and Secretariat drafter Jia Zhi were appointed adjutants to the investiture mission.
units.literal: Jiansu's son E and the Secretariat drafter Jia Zhi were also made adjutants to the investiture mission.
